incidents.vector: Multiple data breaches across the South Korean financial sector; attack methods not yet publicly disclosed
incidents.impact: South Korea's financial regulator ordered sector-wide security reviews following multiple data leaks; full scope of exposed customer data remains unknown.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of unpatched Microsoft SharePoint vulnerabilities for initial access, followed by disabling of endpoint security software and deployment of Warlock ransomware
incidents.impact: Water utility, telecommunications provider, university, and regional government compromised across Europe, Africa, and Latin America; a prior Warlock campaign also struck 400+ organizations including US government agencies.

incidents.vector: Advanced Linux implants — evolved BPFdoor variants and a new AVERAT tool — infected edge email security appliances by mimicking legitimate South Korean (SpamSniper) and Taiwanese (ShareTech) mail gateway software, routing covert C2 traffic over TCP port 25 to blend with normal email traffic
incidents.impact: Long-term persistent access established inside targeted South Korean and Taiwanese telecom networks; implants designed for intelligence collection evade detection by impersonating trusted gateway software and operating with near-zero disk footprint.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of known vulnerabilities in unpatched servers, double-extortion ransomware, and a Ransomware-as-a-Service platform charging $250 affiliate entry fee
incidents.impact: KillSec ransomware group dismantled by Europol following 500+ successful attacks globally since June 2024; three members arrested across Spain, Romania, and the UK; US seeking extradition of the UK-based suspect.

incidents.vector: Ransomware deployed against municipal government IT systems
incidents.impact: City computer systems shut down; utility payment services disrupted for approximately 20,000 residents; FBI and DHS engaged in recovery effort; scope of any data theft under investigation.

incidents.victim: Human rights defenders (targeted via Maroc Telecom)
incidents.vector: Morocco's domestic intelligence agency directed state-owned Maroc Telecom to deploy NSO Group Pegasus spyware against targeted individuals at the network layer, without requiring a device exploit
incidents.impact: Human rights defenders surveilled for four years (2017–2021); exposed by a former intelligence official turned whistleblower; represents a documented case of state-directed telecom infrastructure being used as a spyware delivery mechanism.

incidents.victim: Global financial institutions and governments using SWIFT/SConnect
incidents.vector: Critical RCE vulnerability (CVE-2026-18397, CVSS 9.4) in Thales SConnect browser extension — used for hardware MFA to SWIFT banking, Qatar's national identity system, and the Swedish Tax Agency — exploitable via a drive-by web visit in under 10 seconds
incidents.impact: All 1M+ SConnect users were vulnerable to unauthenticated remote code execution prior to the August/September 2026 patch; product reached end-of-life in June 2026 and many organizations remain unpatched; no confirmed in-the-wild exploitation publicly reported.

incidents.victim: Government and policy organizations across Asia (8 countries)
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing emails with cloned Gmail attachment widgets delivered a multi-stage infection chain; a novel Rust-compiled backdoor using Microsoft 365 / OneDrive as its C2 channel ensured malicious traffic blended with legitimate cloud services
incidents.impact: At least 350 endpoints compromised across 16 environments spanning Taiwan, India, the Philippines, Cambodia, Pakistan, Thailand, Myanmar, and Syria over a 10-month campaign; targets included defense, foreign affairs, legislative, law enforcement, and civil society organizations.

incidents.victim: Global organizations — government, financial, education, telecom
incidents.attacker: Unknown — advanced state-sponsored and criminal groups
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of two critical Citrix NetScaler zero-days (CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, both CVSS 9.5) against internet-facing ADC and Gateway appliances; exploitation began September 3 — three weeks before public disclosure
incidents.impact: Dozens of organizations confirmed compromised across North America and Europe; 50,000+ vulnerable instances exposed on the internet; attackers conducted credential theft, data exfiltration, and lateral movement; CISA, NCSC, and Unit 42 issued emergency advisories.

incidents.victim: Air Traffic and Navigation Services (ATNS), South Africa
incidents.vector: Ransomware deployed to ATNS operational technology (OT) network providing weather services for air traffic control; insider collaboration suspected
incidents.impact: OT systems supporting air traffic weather services disrupted; ATNS manages roughly 6% of global airspace — the attack narrowly avoided crippling both domestic and international air travel across southern Africa.

incidents.victim: AT&T and multiple US telecommunications companies
incidents.vector: Exploitation of Snowflake cloud storage access credentials lacking multi-factor authentication to download call and text metadata records from AT&T and other large telecom providers
incidents.impact: Call and text metadata for tens of millions of AT&T customers stolen; multiple telcos extorted; US Army active-duty soldier Cameron Wagenius sentenced to 70 months in federal prison and ordered to pay $295,000 restitution.

incidents.victim: FBI jobs site and dozens of organizations across multiple sectors
incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of an Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day (CVE-2026-35273, unauthenticated RCE via URL-encoding bypass) against internet-facing PeopleSoft portals across government, higher education, healthcare, technology, agriculture, and transportation
incidents.impact: FBI jobs site breached; SSNs, job details, and psychiatric and medical records of 5,000+ FBI officials stolen; dozens of additional organizations simultaneously compromised in what Mandiant describes as the largest mass-exploitation campaign of 2026.

incidents.vector: Triple zero-day exploit chain: two Chrome JavaScript engine vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-85046, CVE-2026-87491) chained with a Windows ALPC privilege escalation (CVE-2026-85880), delivered via spear-phishing with geopolitical lures on September 3–4
incidents.impact: Multiple Asian government entities targeted; novel CLEANGULP malware family deployed for persistent access; all three CVEs were unpatched at time of exploitation; full scope of compromised environments still being assessed.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to a Pentagon-managed file-sharing server inadvertently exposed on the internet for approximately nine months
incidents.impact: Personal records of 3.1 million US military personnel exposed, including 2.8 million living service members and 294,000 deceased; whether data was actively exfiltrated and by whom remains under investigation.

incidents.vector: AI agents autonomously executed significant portions of the ransomware attack chain — including reconnaissance, vulnerability identification, and lateral movement — with minimal human operator involvement
incidents.impact: Multiple organizations compromised; first publicly documented deployment of autonomous AI agents across an end-to-end ransomware operation, signaling a step-change in attacker productivity; covered in Microsoft's Digital Defense Report 2026.

incidents.vector: Social engineering attack tricking an Odido employee into authenticating on a spoofed website, enabling session hijacking and bulk customer data extraction
incidents.impact: Personal data of more than 6.2 million Dutch citizens stolen; Dutch authorities arrested a suspected member of the extortion group in connection with the breach.
